title: 5. Leading Operational KPIs, Structural Potential & CEO Walk-the-Talk

epigraph.quote: Strategy is what management says on the earnings call; execution is what shows up in capacity utilization, debtor days, and non-anchor OEM wins six quarters later.
epigraph.author: Institutional governance checklist

web_blocks.html: Six leading KPIs cut through quarterly noise. First, track ISG & ISG+EFI adoption across domestic and export 2W/3W platforms. Second, monitor EV MCU (ISAAC) attach rates. Third, watch Industrial CPCB IV+ and export genset share. Fourth, check R&D spend as a % of sales (~6–7%) [13]. Fifth, audit working-capital days (Debtors, Inventory, Payables) [1]. Sixth, verify plant utilization across MF1, MF3, MF4, and MF5 [5].

web_blocks.takeaway: Operational health passes with active monitoring: Mobility volume velocity (1.45M Q2 ECUs, >5M cumulative scooter controllers, European OEM win) is firing strongly, but H1 FY27 Industrial contraction (-21.8% YoY), negative H1 CFO (-₹20.38 Cr), and heavy MF3/MF5 capex require strict execution discipline [1, 5].

web_blocks.html: SEDEMAC's addressable market extends well beyond domestic scooters. Management's H1 FY27 roadmap highlights five growth legs [5]. First, export three-wheeler ISG ECUs and variant motorcycle models for domestic OEMs. Second, a new European 2W/3W OEM ISG & magneto kit contract (SoP H1 FY28) [5]. Third, wet-magneto ISG kits for FY28 production. Fourth, EV traction MCUs (ISAAC) and electric machines (MF4) [9]. Fifth, CPCB IV+ industrial EFI controllers [8]. MF3 triples Chakan plant space, while MF5 (Shoolagiri) adds South Indian OEM proximity [5].

web_blocks.title: CEO & Management Walk-the-Talk Audit (MD Prof. Shashikanth Suryanarayanan, JMD Amit Dixit & CFO Rajesh Sheth)
paragraphs: Verbatim Q2 FY27 Earnings Call Record (Nov 3, 2026; Filed Nov 11, 2026) [5, 39]: On PCB and raw-material margin pressure, Managing Director Prof. Shashikanth Suryanarayanan stated candidly: “First of all, there is no pass-through. It is negotiated broadly... in the current environment, there is an ongoing negotiation on increase in prices.” On MF3 capacity ramp, he added: “The primary motivation for building new plants is to free up some space and also the chaos that comes with very high utilization... Over the next couple of quarters, if we fully populated it and maintain the same revenue that we are at this point in time, then we will be at about 65%-70% utilization.” Addressing H1 working-capital buildup (₹135 Cr to ₹258 Cr), he remarked: “First of all, working capital has not substantially increased on a percentage terms to revenue... working capital increases primarily because of revenue increase... So, we do not see this situation substantially changing”—adding on debt discipline: “Our aim is to make sure that our debt-to-equity ratio is healthy.”

Joint Managing Director & CFO Disclosure [39]: Joint Managing Director Amit Arun Dixit delivered the financial slides, warning: “Going ahead, we expect even more pressure also to come on account of cost increase on PCBs... Overall, we expect our EBITDA to hold for H2, as compared to H1 FY 2027,” while guiding H2 capex lower: “at least for the H2, it will be lower than what it has been for H1, primarily because our MF3, the CapEx for the MF3 will come down. It is nearly ready.” Chief Financial Officer Rajesh Madhukar Sheth is listed as a management participant on the official Q2 FY27 transcript cover sheet filed with BSE/NSE [39], but he did not deliver separate verbatim speaking remarks during the published Q&A transcript (JMD Amit Dixit presented the financial deck and MD Prof. Suryanarayanan answered balance-sheet and borrowing questions).

What Management Delivered vs. Where Skepticism Remains Warranted: Leadership scaled revenue 4.4x from ₹240 Cr (FY21) to ₹1,058 Cr (FY26), crossed 5 million cumulative scooter controllers and 1 million ISG+EFI units, won a European 2W/3W OEM program (SoP H1 FY28), and earned an India Ratings IND A/Stable upgrade [1, 5, 39]. Yet skepticism remains essential: TVS Motor still drives ~75–81% of sales [6, 13], H1 Industrial fell -21.8% pushing Mobility to 91.1% [5], the March 2026 IPO was a 100% OFS bringing ₹0 fresh equity, and Prof. Suryanarayanan's admission that working-capital intensity will not substantially reverse in H2 makes restoring positive CFO and FCF—while lifting MF3 toward 65%–70% utilization and holding H2 EBITDA margins near ~19%—the decisive governance test [1, 5, 39].

book_paragraphs: Once you understand what a company makes and how its unit economics work, the next job is deciding which dashboard gauges actually matter. With SEDEMAC, watching quarterly net profit alone is like driving by looking only at the speedometer while ignoring the oil pressure. You need six leading operational KPIs on your screen.

First is ISG and ISG+EFI penetration alongside non-TVS OEM diversification. Today, ISG-related ECUs bring in roughly 60% to 64% or more of revenue, and TVS Motor writes roughly 75% to 81% of the checks. Execution velocity in Mobility is undeniable—SEDEMAC shipped a record 1.45 million control-intensive ECUs in Q2 FY27 (+37.5% YoY), crossed 5 million cumulative scooter motor controllers in October 2026, and won a European two/three-wheeler OEM ISG ECU and magneto kit contract slated for H1 FY28 start of production. The KPI to watch is simple: does TVS concentration steadily step down toward 60% and 50% over the next three years as Bajaj, Hero, export three-wheeler, and European programs scale?

Second is the commercial attach rate of EV Motor Control Units. Moving from 0.3% of mobility revenue in FY24 to roughly 6% of total revenue in 9M FY26—and ramping MF4's electric-machine shipments starting Q3 FY27—is encouraging, though SEDEMAC must defend share against Sterling Tools, Lucas-TVS, and Minda Corporation. Third is Industrial genset growth—a gauge that just flashed amber: after surging 55% in FY26 to ₹146 crore on CPCB IV+ upgrades, Industrial contracted 21.8% YoY in H1 FY27 to ₹63.02 crore (with Q2 segment profit down 33.9% YoY). Fourth is R&D intensity, which has stayed around 6% to 7% of sales; in deep-tech controls, cutting R&D to flatter a single quarter's margin is eating your seed corn.

Fifth and sixth are the two balance-sheet gauges flashing amber right now: working-capital days and plant utilization. Debtor days stretched from 24 days in FY25 to 46.1 days in FY26, trade receivables jumped to ₹212.16 crore and inventories to ₹287.81 crore by September 2026, pushing H1 FY27 operating cash flow negative at -₹20.38 crore. At the same time, MF1 is maxed out above 90% utilization, MF3's 120,000-square-foot Chakan plant just entered pilot production, and MF5 land has been acquired in Shoolagiri.

How do Managing Director Prof. Shashikanth Suryanarayanan, Joint Managing Director Amit Dixit, and Chief Financial Officer Rajesh Madhukar Sheth score on a walk-the-talk audit of the November 3, 2026 Q2 FY27 earnings call transcript? Give them genuine credit for operational delivery and candor. Prof. Suryanarayanan openly acknowledged that electronics inputs lack automatic indexation—stating verbatim, 'First of all, there is no pass-through. It is negotiated broadly... in the current environment, there is an ongoing negotiation on increase in prices'—and explained the MF3 expansion clearly: 'The primary motivation for building new plants is to free up some space and also the chaos that comes with very high utilization... Over the next couple of quarters, if we fully populated it and maintain the same revenue that we are at this point in time, then we will be at about 65%-70% utilization.' JMD Amit Dixit, who led the financial presentation, warned directly that 'we expect even more pressure also to come on account of cost increase on PCBs' while projecting H2 EBITDA to hold versus H1 and H2 capex to taper because MF3 is 'nearly ready.' Notably, while CFO Rajesh Madhukar Sheth is listed on the official BSE/NSE transcript cover sheet, he did not deliver separate verbatim speaking remarks during the published Q&A; Prof. Suryanarayanan handled the borrowing and working-capital questions himself, stating that 'working capital increases primarily because of revenue increase... So, we do not see this situation substantially changing' and that 'our aim is to make sure that our debt-to-equity ratio is healthy.' That frank admission—that elevated working capital will persist alongside 40%+ growth following a 100% OFS IPO—underscores why MF3 utilization and H2 cash conversion remain our primary governance exam.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Management has earned high marks for engineering execution and candor on margin headwinds, but the next 18 months are a capital-allocation exam: ramping MF3 without letting debt-funded working capital erode returns on capital.

book_subsections.title: The TAM Runway: Domestic 2W/3W, Global Gensets, and EV Powertrains
paragraphs: When you step back from quarterly numbers and ask how large SEDEMAC can become over a five-to-ten-year horizon, the addressable runway breaks into three concentric rings. The inner ring is domestic and export two- and three-wheeler ICE micro-hybridization, where silent-start ISG and OBD Stage II-B EFI continue penetrating commuter motorcycles, export three-wheelers, and a newly won European 2W/3W OEM program (SoP H1 FY28). The middle ring is electric two- and three-wheelers plus cordless power tools, where sensorless MCUs (ISAAC) and rare-earth-free motors (Logan) let SEDEMAC capture higher electronic content per vehicle as powertrains electrify under PM E-DRIVE localisation rules. The outer ring is global industrial gensets, where CPCB IV+ compliance in India and gas/diesel EFI adoption in North America expand content per generator—even though H1 FY27's 21.8% YoY pullback proves industrial demand arrives in cyclical waves.

What separates real TAM capture from slide-deck TAM is qualification velocity. Every new OEM platform takes 18 to 36 months of co-development before volume shipments begin. That is why tracking non-TVS design wins, MF3 utilization ramp toward 65%–70%, Industrial stabilization, and EV MCU revenue share tells you far more about 2028 earnings power than any single quarter's top-line surprise.
